Name: Equity-Driven AI in Public Policy
Title: Balancing Equity and Efficiency: Evaluating Machine Learning vs Bureaucratic Expansion in Social Welfare Distribution
Problem: Can machine learning predictions enhance the equity of welfare resource distribution compared to expanding bureaucratic capacity in addressing long-term unemployment in Germany? This question is crucial as long-term unemployment remains a persistent issue, affecting nearly 41% of the unemployed population in Germany as of 2022 (OECD Employment Outlook 2019). Current bureaucratic processes are often criticized for inefficiency and bias, resulting in uneven resource allocation. Investigating whether AI can provide a more equitable solution is vital for policymakers seeking effective strategies.
Importance: The importance of this research lies in the potential to revolutionize social welfare distribution using AI, addressing inefficiencies and biases inherent in traditional methods. Given that Germany's long-term unemployment rate significantly impacts economic productivity and social stability, optimizing resource distribution can lead to substantial societal benefits (OECD Employment Outlook 2019). Furthermore, as AI integration into public policy is accelerating, understanding its implications on equity is urgent, as highlighted in 'Artificial Intelligence and the Good Society'.
Difficulty: (1) Data Quality and Availability: Welfare data is often incomplete or sensitive, posing a challenge for accurate machine learning predictions. (2) Bias and Fairness Challenges: AI systems must address biases that can skew outcomes, as discussed in 'Towards a standard for identifying and managing bias in artificial intelligence'. (3) Policy Integration Complexity: Integrating AI into existing bureaucratic frameworks involves technical, legal, and cultural barriers. (4) Evaluation Metrics: Traditional metrics may not capture equity nuances, necessitating new measurement tools that align with policy objectives.
NoveltyComparison: Previous studies, such as 'The Value of Prediction in Identifying the Worst-Off', focus on AI's predictive power in social services but lack a comparative analysis with bureaucratic methods. 'Harmonizing Intelligence' addresses bias in AI but doesn't compare AI outcomes with traditional approaches. Our research fills this gap by directly comparing AI-driven and bureaucratic methods in resource distribution, focusing on both predictive performance and equity of outcomes. Unlike prior work, this study offers a holistic view of the trade-offs involved, providing critical insights for policymakers.
Approach: (1) Develop machine learning models using unemployment data to identify individuals most at risk of long-term unemployment, employing data augmentation and fairness-aware algorithms to mitigate bias and scarcity issues. (2) Simulate bureaucratic expansion using an agent-based model to manage unemployment resources, providing a baseline for comparison with AI methods. (3) Evaluate both strategies using advanced equity measurement tools, such as distribution fairness indices and novel impact metrics, addressing the challenge of capturing nuances in equity beyond traditional accuracy measures. This approach ensures a rigorous analysis of the identified difficulties, offering a comprehensive examination of AI's potential in public policy.

Dataset.Name: ag_news
Dataset.Preprocessing: Text lowercasing and TF-IDF vectorization to 128 dimensions

Metric.Justification: Accuracy and F1 Score for prediction performance; Equity Gap Metric for distribution fairness.
